app.title: LabChronicle | Database Visualizer
app.summary: A person loads a lab's records, either a bundled example or a GitHub repository of YAML files, and picks one database: reagents, cell lines, animal models, experiments or publications. They narrow the table with per-field filters in the sidebar and a global search that accepts several comma-separated terms, then tick rows to mark them. They can open any record in a detail card, which for experiments includes a generated description, and add it to the selection from there. The marked rows export as a CSV or PDF list, with links back to each record's source file.

task.text: Find records of a lab's reagents, cell lines, models, experiments and publications in one place, and export a selected list of them.

data.text: A lab's records kept as YAML files in a repository: reagents with catalogue, storage, dilution and stock-status fields; cell lines; animal models; experiments stored on hard drives; and publications whose figures point back to experiments. All of it is flattened into one table per database.
data.item: one record in a lab database, such as an antibody, a cell line, an experiment or a publication

stage.text: keeping lab inventory and experiment records findable during ongoing bench work

mechanism.text: Sidebar filter widgets, made from a per-database field config, and a global search narrow a read-only table that has a checkbox column for selecting rows. A record chosen in the detail card, or the row last ticked in the table, opens with every field shown. The accumulated selection goes to CSV or PDF export.

field.text: lab inventory and research data management in cell biology

workflow.name: search a record collection and export a selected list

steps.here: Load the bundled example database, or clone a public or private GitHub repository using a token. The YAML files are flattened into tables, and storage box IDs are replaced by box names.

steps.step: choose which collection to work in
steps.here: A dropdown switches between Antibodies, Cell Lines, Plasmids, Animal Models, Dyes, Small Molecules, siRNAs, Experiments and Publications. Each has its own columns, and a mobile view shows fewer of them.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Sidebar filters are generated per database: text boxes, multiselects over values (list values are unpacked), date-range sliders, and number sliders for numeric columns such as the publication figure count.
A global search keeps rows where any field contains the text, ignoring case. Comma-separated terms match any of them.
Tick the Select checkbox on rows, or use Select all rows and Clear selection. The selection is kept per database even when filters hide rows, and the count of selected rows is shown.
The Show Full Record Details panel lists every field in two columns. Experiments get a generated description with links to their metadata files. A button adds the record to the table selection.
The CSV and PDF buttons, disabled until rows are selected, download the selected rows with readable column names. The source YAML file becomes a link into the repository.

distinctive: Records live as YAML files in a git repository, and every exported row links back to its source file on the current branch.
Storage locations are stored as box IDs and shown as human-readable freezer or rack names taken from a boxes file.
Experiments are indexed by the hard drive and folder where their raw data sits. Publications list the experiments behind each figure panel.
Reagent records carry stock status (tube state, reorder flag, last checked date) and per-application dilution and validation fields that can be filtered.
A mobile view trims each database to a few key columns.
